clue.text: Unsettled strike-breaker in Morecambe?

indicators.note: the strike-breaker is placed in the comedian's first name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise; the question mark flags the first name by example
a rat is a worker who breaks a strike, a scab

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker turns up in a northern seaside town and stirs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort, but it stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe; RAT goes inside ERIC after ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsettled is irregular and unpredictable, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Surrealist birds heading to the south

indicators.note: in a down clue south is the bottom, so the first letter of the birds goes to the end

parts.note: terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Birds fly south in a surreal scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German painter of the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Rolls back snooker balls to snatch victory

indicators.note: the snooker balls grab the victory and hold it inside

parts.note: the reds are the fifteen red balls in snooker
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Snooker balls roll back as a player snatches the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding tape or film back to the start rolls it back.

clue.text: Hathaway's return to friendliness

indicators.note: the 's stands for 'has', so the name contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Anne Hathaway goes back to being friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests reading backwards, but the letters run forwards in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: When frosty relations warm up and soften, they are said to melt, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Sort of architect: Henry E Holden's occupation?

indicators.note: sort means arrange, so the letters of architect and Henry E are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An architect called Henry E Holden, and what kind of work he does.
explanation.walkthrough: Holden Caulfield, Salinger's narrator, dreams of the job in the novel's title: catching children before they run off a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: In Salinger's novel Holden imagines his ideal job is this, saving playing children from falling.

clue.text: Bible editor includes sin alleged as fact

indicators.note: the Bible and editor pieces together hold the sin inside them

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: An editor of scripture allows a sinful passage to be presented as fact.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something firmly as true is to assert it; past tense matches the clue's past participle.

clue.text: Burl Ives almost recalled twisted seducer

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A twisted villain recalls the singer Burl Ives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the S from Burl Ives; with RECALLED the letters BURLIVE are rearranged by 'twisted'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles he is the villain who seduces Tess.

clue.text: Stout eastern doctor leading unit

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
on can mean ahead, as a team leading by goals is so many on
a point is a unit, as in typesetting or scoring

explanation.surface: A stout doctor from the east heading a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term means plumpness, so a stout figure is described by it.

clue.text: Dish is extravagant served in rhino's hide

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the rhino's skin
a hide is the outer skin, so the first and last letters of rhino are taken

parts.note: OTT means over the top, extravagant

explanation.surface: An extravagant meal served in rhino skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Howl in Little Wing to render intelligible?

indicators.note: the howl is placed in the little wing

parts.note: a department is a wing of an organisation; little means abbreviated
to howl is to cry out

explanation.surface: Screams in Hendrix's song Little Wing, to make sense of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode an encrypted message is to make it readable.

clue.text: Recently discovered citadel in place on 11

parts.note: something recently found is new
a citadel is a fortress, a castle

explanation.surface: A newly unearthed fortress in a town by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the answer at 11 across, the river on which this northern English city stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The city stands on the river that is the answer to 11 across, so it is a place on it.

clue.text: Primary ABC is revised

indicators.note: revised text is reworked, so the letters of ABC IS are rearranged

explanation.surface: A primary-school alphabet book has been updated.
explanation.definitionFit: Primary and fundamental are synonyms: the first, most elementary level.

clue.text: Some activity near river

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: There is a bit of activity close to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the river of north-east England that flows through Newcastle.

clue.text: Christie's style juggling round with Doyle's central character

indicators.note: juggling throws things around, so the letters of ROUND WITH are rearranged
the letter at the very centre of the name Doyle is taken

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's way of writing juggles plots around with Conan Doyle's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central character' suggests Sherlock Holmes, but it means only the middle letter Y of DOYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie wrote murder mysteries, so her style is the craft of the detective puzzle story.

clue.text: Last of Mohicans below ground in place on 24

indicators.note: the final letter of Mohicans is taken

parts.note: below means under
land is ground, the earth

explanation.surface: The Last of the Mohicans buried below ground near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 24 down, the river that flows through this north-east English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city stands on the river that is the answer to 24 down.

clue.text: One to license is one to institute legal proceedings

parts.note: a person who brings a lawsuit is someone who sues

explanation.surface: A licensing authority is also the party that may take you to court.
explanation.definitionFit: The body that grants a licence hands it out, a sense of giving out official documents.

clue.text: Operatic role thought to release energy

indicators.note: release means let go, so the energy is removed

parts.note: an idea is a thought
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An opera singer believes the part lets loose energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The title princess of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Princess Ida.

clue.text: Rook loves hawk to destroy totally

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
love is zero in tennis, O; two of them give OO
to hawk goods is to tout them, sell aggressively

explanation.surface: A rook is keen to wipe out a hawk completely.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook and hawk both look like birds; here one is a chess piece and the other a verb meaning to peddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate something completely is to extirpate it from its very base, an idiom.

clue.text: European support for British instrument

indicators.note: in a down answer the European piece sits under British, holding it up

parts.note: UK stands for the United Kingdom, Britain

explanation.surface: European backing for a British musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar-like instrument.

clue.text: Champion's boy in distress

indicators.note: the boy sits inside the distress

parts.note: pain is suffering or distress
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A champion is a boy in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A chivalrous knight who fights for a cause is a champion; Charlemagne's twelve peers bore the name.

clue.text: He wrote something good about gold pot, finally

indicators.note: the something good goes round the gold and last letter

parts.note: a plus is an advantage, something good
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of pot is taken

explanation.surface: A writer produced something good about a pot of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Roman playwright wrote Aulularia, a comedy about a pot of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman comic playwright, so a man who wrote.

clue.text: Bird coming in on duck showed forbearance

indicators.note: the bird enters the cricket side

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a tit is a small bird
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A bird landing on a duck that tolerated it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word but is the cricket term: the on side is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a matter and not pursue it is to show patience and forbearance; past tense matches.

clue.text: Girl, English, posh, lovely

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh, in British usage
nice means pleasant, lovely

explanation.surface: A description of a pleasant, well-spoken English girl.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' distinction of upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so a girl's name stands for any girl.

clue.text: Parisian dear carries weapon for sweet talker

indicators.note: the French word holds the weapon inside it

parts.note: cher is French for dear
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A Parisian sweetheart packing a gun to win over others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smooth and persuasive who wins people over with flattery.

clue.text: Man's application to eat pudding first

indicators.note: the pudding is placed at the front of the answer, before the eating

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the course after the main
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: A man asks to eat dessert before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented lotion applied after shaving is a typical men's grooming product.

clue.text: Mother goddess in northern vale?

definitions.meaning: a Buddhist female deity, the mother of liberation
vale is Latin for farewell; northern English dialect has a colloquial goodbye of these letters

explanation.surface: A mother goddess living in a valley in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vale' looks like a valley, but it is Latin for goodbye, and the question mark signals that twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: a Tibetan Buddhist goddess and a Northern English farewell, cheerio.

clue.text: Dominant mountain a height to climb

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upwards, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A dominant mountain, a peak to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: The top-ranking animal in a group, so a dominant one, is so called.

clue.text: Use River Don

definitions.meaning: to use clothes until they are worn out
the river that flows through Durham and Sunderland
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Use the River Don.
explanation.walkthrough: The Don is a real Yorkshire river, but here it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: to put on clothes, to use up, and a river in north-east England.

clue.text: Mashed tater and fish

indicators.note: mashed potato is broken up, so the letters of tater are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plate of mashed potato with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tater is informal for potato, which suits 'Mashed' on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brightly coloured tropical freshwater species kept in aquariums.

clue.text: Rise and Fall here charted?

parts.note: reads like the history of an empire's rise and fall, but describes a map showing hills and valleys in raised form

explanation.surface: A history book charting the rise and fall of a power.
explanation.definitionFit: A map that shows terrain heights, so the ups and downs of the land are charted on it.

clue.text: Foot of water in bishop's office

indicators.note: the water is placed in the bishop's office

parts.note: a see is the seat or diocese of a bishop
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: A foot of water has flooded the bishop's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is a metrical foot of verse, not a measure of depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two long syllables in classical verse.

clue.text: Film and sport broadcast about pots made here

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an alien
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the broadcast word is read backwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A film and a sports broadcast about pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the Stoke-on-Trent site of Josiah Wedgwood's pottery works.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood's factory district in Stoke-on-Trent, named after ancient Etruscan pottery, where pots were made.
